title: podman machine start hangs forever on its final ssh check and leaves "Starting":true
body:
## Summary

`podman machine start` does not return on my machine. It brings the machine up
correctly -- by the time it hangs, both Docker API pipes answer -- and then blocks
forever on the last thing the start does: a `ssh ... true` check run through podman's
built-in Go SSH client. Killing it leaves `"Starting":true` in the machine config, so
`podman machine list` then reports "Currently starting" indefinitely.

## Where it hangs

With `--log-level=debug`:

    API forwarding listening on: npipe:////./pipe/docker_engine
    Docker API clients default to this address. ...
    time=... level=debug msg="Running ssh command on machine \"podman-machine-default\": true"
    <never returns>

That message comes from podman's built-in Go SSH client (`localhostBuiltinSSH` in
`pkg/machine/ssh.go`, using `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` rather than shelling out to
`ssh`). It opens a session, runs `true`, and waits for the server to close the channel.

## Why it does not return

The machine's sshd is **OpenSSH 10.2p1**. Against it the exec is accepted
(`exec request accepted on channel 0`) but no exit-status/close ever arrives. The
server is not simply broken:

- the Windows `ssh.exe` (OpenSSH 9.5p2) hangs on the same
  `ssh -i <identity> -p <port> user@localhost true`, over `::1` or `127.0.0.1` alike;
- a Linux OpenSSH 9.6p1 client runs the identical exec against the same forwarded
  socket and returns `0` immediately;
- sshd logs `Accepted publickey ... session opened` and never `session closed`;
- forcing the cipher, MAC, KEX, host-key algorithm or compression, or adding `-tt`,
  changes nothing.

So this looks like an interop stall between that server and the clients that run here,
and I accept it may not reproduce against a stock server. podman's behaviour is still a
bug: the check has no timeout, so `machine start` waits forever instead of failing, and
because it never reaches the end of its own start sequence it never writes
`"Starting":false` either.

## What I would ask for

- give the machine SSH checks a timeout and surface an error instead of blocking
  forever; and
- reset `"Starting"` when a start fails or is interrupted, so a bad start does not
  leave the machine permanently reported as "Currently starting".

## Environment

podman 6.0.2 (client) on Windows; WSL 3.0.1.0 (kernel 6.18.40.1-1);
`podman-machine-default`, `WSLHypervisor.UserModeNetworking=true`; ssh forwarded on
`127.0.0.1:7853`; machine sshd OpenSSH 10.2p1. The machine's sshd is stock.

[24416]: https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/24416
